meta.description: Infer large-scale copy-number alterations from tumor single-cell or single-nucleus RNA-seq to separate malignant from normal cells and call subclones using inferCNV, copyKAT, SCEVAN, and Numbat.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated studies, identifiers, effect sizes, or clinical claims appeared.

practice_boundaries.detail: Clinical-certainty requests were refused; outputs remain research-analysis guidance.

methodological_ground.detail: Outputs preserve normal-reference, per-patient, resolution, and orthogonal-validation requirements.

code_usability.detail: Fresh inferCNV, copyKAT, Numbat validation, SCEVAN, and selector executions completed with checkable assertions.

functional_suitability.note: All four advertised CNV routes have actionable method selection, inputs, commands, and interpretation limits.

reliability.note: Reference selection, sex, cell-cycle, HLA/Ig, and SCEVAN plotting failures have explicit recovery advice.

performance_context.note: The 257-line main file is concise for four methods; Numbat preprocessing remains necessarily substantial.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, goals, parameter table, and common-error table make branch selection clear.

human_usability.note: The short usage guide defers operational detail to SKILL.md without duplicating it.

security.note: No credentials, destructive commands, or unfiltered code execution were found.

maintainability.note: Two shipped examples cover the nontrivial inferCNV and SCEVAN pathways; external packages remain version-sensitive.

agent_specific.note: Trigger language is specific, progressive disclosure is clear, and the Skill offers safe exit conditions.

copyKAT documentation correctly retains hg20; version 1.2.5 exposes hg20 and mm10 branches, not hg19.

Shipped SCEVAN and inferCNV examples are aligned with observed current-package behavior.
